newsitem.title: UK: Sterling Eurobonds steady on British election day.
newsitem.headline: Sterling Eurobonds steady on British election day.

text.p: There was little trade in sterling Eurobonds on Thursday as Britain took to the polls in an election that is expected to topple the Conservative government after 18 years of rule.
Many trading desks will be fully staffed by 0500 GMT on Friday, but dealers said they were expecting little activity in the Eurosterling sector until late morning on Friday at the earliest.
"Investors will do their government (gilt) business first, and then concentrate on Eurobonds," a dealer at a British bank said.
"There won't be a clear indication of what the Eurobond market's reaction is to the election results until late morning or early afternoon (Friday)," he said.
The sector's ten-year benchmark, a European Investment Bank (EIB) 7.625 percent 2007 bond, was trading at around 10 basis points over gilts at 1245 GMT.
An Export-Import Bank of Japan (Exim) 8.00 percent 2007 bond was quoted at 20/18 b.p. over.
Both had tightened by around two notches this week, dealers said.
Spreads on shorter-dated paper had not moved. The five-year benchmark, a Fannie Mae 6.875 percent 2002 bond, was trading at around 11.5 b.p. over.

"It is absolutely dead today," a Eurosterling trader at another British bank said. "We have seen some buying of 10-year paper this week, but activity won't resume until after the election results are known."
Opinion polls are predicting a clear victory for the main opposition Labour party. A Reuters survey of political experts predicted a 92-seat majority in parliament for Labour.
"If Labour gets a 200-seat majority, or only a 10-seat majority, there will be a strong reaction from the markets," another Eurosterling trader said.
"We expect the market to remain steady if the results are as predicted."
A combination of holidays in Europe and Japan, and the advent of a long week-end in Britain, might also mute the market's reaction, he said.
Eurosterling price moves will be determined by the direction of gilts, and whether or not spreads tighten depend on sterling's reaction to the election results.

"Eurosterling prices shadow gilt prices," a trader said. "Whether investors buy or sell their sterling holdings will depend on their view of the currency -- if it is seen to be weakening we could see selling and spread widening," he said.

Investor appetite for sterling Eurobonds, especially from continental Europe, surged in 1997 on the back of a strong pound. More than $26 billion equivalent of new bonds were launched in the first quarter of 1997, compared with $14 billion in the first quarter of 1996.
Gilts rallied on Wednesday, with the June long gilt future gaining a further 1/8 point on Thursday to open at 110-23/32. Sterling was holding steady in quiet trade.
